title: Majestic King
summary: Save the bishop rather than the knight, then use a king detour to turn a pawn race into mate.

nodes.question: Which minor piece does White need to keep?
nodes.explanation: The knight is attacked by Kd7 and Black’s knight threatens b2. The forcing Nb6 check reveals a choice between keeping a knight and keeping a bishop.

nodes.question: Can the king help while moving away from the pawn?
nodes.explanation: White has sacrificed the knight and kept the dark-squared bishop. Ke6 creates a route toward c4, where the king and bishop can build a mating net around Ka4.

branches.title: Save the bishop and build a mating net
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece source board and follow the selected king-retreat defense.
Nb6+ checks Kd7 and attacks the knight on a4, forcing Black to respond before taking b2.
Kc6 avoids capturing the knight and sets up a counterfork after White takes a4.
Nxa4 removes Black’s knight but brings the white knight close to the bishop.
Kb5 attacks both Na4 and Ba5. White must choose which minor piece to save.
Bc3 saves the bishop and allows the knight to fall. The bishop’s long diagonal will matter more than the knight.
Kxa4 captures the knight and places the black king in the cage that White will exploit.
Ke6 moves toward the c4 mating construction rather than chasing h5 directly.
h4 races toward promotion. This is the source’s selected pawn-running defense.
Kd5 approaches c4 while keeping the bishop on its useful diagonal.
h3 continues the race, apparently outpacing the white king.
Kc4 reaches the crucial square and confines Ka4 with help from b2 and the bishop.
h2 leaves Black one step from obtaining a queen.
Bb4 controls a5 and sets up b3 mate. Promotion will not provide a useful defense.
h1=Q promotes far from the mating cage; the queen cannot stop b3.
b3# is actual mate. Kc4 protects b3 and b4, Bb4 checks Ka4 and covers a5, while the new queen has no legal way to answer.
branches.explanation: b3# is actual mate. Kc4 protects b3 and b4, Bb4 checks Ka4 and covers a5, while the new queen has no legal way to answer.

branches.title: Black captures the checking knight
commentary: Compare the source’s direct knight exchange rather than the king counterfork.
Nb6+ forks the king and Na4, making Black respond.
Nxb6 removes the checking knight but leaves a bishop recapture.
Bxb6 wins Black’s knight. The exact bishop-and-pawn versus pawn ending is winning for White; the source’s further king race is not encoded here.
branches.explanation: Bxb6 wins Black’s knight. The exact bishop-and-pawn versus pawn ending is winning for White; the source’s further king race is not encoded here.

branches.title: Save the knight instead of the bishop
commentary: Compare keeping the knight when Black forks the two white pieces.
Nb6+ starts the same forcing sequence.
Kc6 prepares the king counterfork.
Nxa4 wins Black’s knight but places both white minors within the king’s reach.
Kb5 attacks the knight and bishop together.
Nc3+ saves the knight with check but gives up the forced win.
Kxa5 removes the bishop. The exact remaining knight-and-pawn ending is drawn with best play; no invented pawn-race completion is required.
branches.explanation: Kxa5 removes the bishop. The exact remaining knight-and-pawn ending is drawn with best play; no invented pawn-race completion is required.

exercises.prompt: Why does the king move toward e6 instead of chasing h5?
exercises.answer: The useful destination is c4. With the bishop and b-pawn, that king position builds mate around Ka4 even if the distant pawn promotes.
The bishop can help create the mating cage. Saving the knight instead permits ...Kxa5 and leaves an exactly drawn ending.

startContext: The complete seven-piece source board is visually reconstructed. The selected ...Kc6/...Kb5 counterfork, bishop-preserving king detour, direct knight exchange and wrong-piece comparison are checked move by move. The mating race is one illustrated defense; the lesson does not claim to enumerate every king and pawn alternative.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
